articles.title: The 8 tests I ship in a starter kit (and why I stop at 8)
articles.excerpt: Most starter kits ship with one test: test_that_true_is_true. It's the Laravel default, and almost nobody replaces it. When I started packing my SaaS kit for other developers, I decided the test suite…
articles.body: Most starter kits ship with one test: test_that_true_is_true . It's the Laravel default, and almost nobody replaces it. When I started packing my SaaS kit for other developers, I decided the test suite had to earn its place — a buyer should be able to run php artisan test , watch green, and trust that the auth layer they just bought actually works. So the kit ships tests/Feature/AuthTest.php with eight real tests. Here's what they cover and why each one exists. The register tests. test_register_returns_token_and_user posts to /api/auth/register and asserts a 201 with a user object (shaped through the API resource) and a token . It also asserts the database row was created with role => 'user' — because the register endpoint hardcodes the role.

articles.body: your dashboard's biggest traffic source is probably called direct. which is a polite way of saying nobody knows where it came from. i'm om yaduvanshi, 18, an applied ai developer building cloudline , a cookieless analytics tool. day 20 of 90, building in public. what "direct" actually is people hear "direct" and picture someone typing their url. a small slice is that. most of it is traffic the referrer system never identified. messaging apps that strip referrers. social apps opening links in in-app browsers. newsletters with no tracking tags. ai assistants that send people your way and never tell you. your biggest traffic source is a shrug with a name. the problem i ran into when i built cloudline's traffic-sources view, direct kept winning. top bucket on my own sites.

articles.title: Handing your download store to a helper: a least-access handover playbook for sellers who finally aren't doing it all alone
articles.excerpt: Most download stores start as one person doing everything: making the file, writing the page, answering the "I never got my download" email at midnight. The first help usually arrives informally — a p…
articles.body: Most download stores start as one person doing everything: making the file, writing the page, answering the "I never got my download" email at midnight. The first help usually arrives informally — a partner, a friend, a part-time assistant hired off a job board — and the handover usually happens the worst possible way: one message containing every password you own. It feels generous and efficient. It is neither. A helper with total access can accidentally refund the wrong buyer, delete the canonical file, or send a broken link to fifty people, and none of that requires bad intentions — only a bad afternoon and no boundaries.

articles.body: Earlier this week, a mass hack of refrigeration systems at an estimated 700 supermarkets throughout France caused them to suddenly malfunction, causing spoilage of untold tons of perishables and, in some cases, fires. As is now the norm, basic cybersecurity would have prevented it. French authorities say the systems, made up of entire fleets of refrigerators and freezers throughout a store, were hacked. More specifically, Internet-connected controllers that allow technicians to remotely administer the store-wide systems were compromised. The unknown attackers responsible then activated defrosters long enough for the fridges to reach temperatures as high as 50° Celsius (122° Fahrenheit).

articles.title: Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 ‘families,’ scientists find
articles.excerpt: Scientists have performed a cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems.
articles.body: You can tell a lot about how a child will age by looking at their parents, and it turns out that this could be true for planetary systems, too. Scientists have performed cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems. The study team, led by researchers at the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), studied 300 of the best-understood multiplanet systems of the over 1,000 that astronomers have discovered in the Milky Way. The team's research clarifies how the environments around infant stars directly affect planetary fates and, in turn, the survival of extrasolar planets, or exoplanets , that are potentially capable of hosting life.

articles.title: The AI race is back on
articles.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg at the Meta Connect developer conference. | Photo: Andrej Sokolow/dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves,…
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg at the Meta Connect developer conference. | Photo: Andrej Sokolow/dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models that left their rivals in the dust. Google seemed hopelessly far behind, while Meta, despite spending billions to revive its floundering AI ambitions , had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. Even the latest models coming out of China , impressive as they were, appeared to be playing catch-up. Then, in the space of a few days, everything changed. Google and Meta both unveiled frontier models they claim can go toe to toe with the best from OpenAI and Anthropic.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship just turned 10 years old. When will it go to Mars?
articles.excerpt: A decade after Elon Musk publicly unveiled plans for the fully reusable megarocket, Starship has reached orbit. How far away is Mars?
articles.body: Starship just reached orbit for the first time, carrying satellites for SpaceX's Starlink program. Analysts disagree on whether that's a detour or the destination — and what of the company's plans for the Red Planet? Ten years ago, Elon Musk stood on stage at the International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Guadalajara, Mexico, and unveiled plans for a giant spaceship to carry people to Mars. This past Sept. 28 — a decade and a day later — the descendant of that vehicle reached orbit for the first time , on Starship's 14th-ever test flight. The designs and hardware evolved greatly over those 10 years.

articles.title: NASA’s Chandra Breaks Down ‘Treble Clef’s’ Galaxy Cluster Collision
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have used NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory to break down the cause of a remarkable formation of radio waves they have nicknamed the “Treble Clef” because its distinct shape strongly resemb…
articles.body: X-ray: NASA/CXC/INAF-IRA/A. Botteon et al.; Infrared: UKIDSS-GPS ; Radio: ASTRON/LOFAR; Image processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/N. Wolk Astronomers have used NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory to break down the cause of a remarkable formation of radio waves they have nicknamed the “Treble Clef” because its distinct shape strongly resembles the musical symbol. The researchers discovered the Treble Clef is likely caused by an outburst from a supermassive black hole, followed by a collision of two galaxy clusters. A paper describing the findings, led by Andrea Botteon of the National Institute for Astrophysics, or INAF, in Italy, published Wednesday in the Astronomy & Astrophysics journal .

articles.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
articles.excerpt: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
articles.body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered.
